summary: The TaiwanICDF International Higher Education Scholarship Program is run by the Taiwan International Cooperation and Development Fund together with partner universities in the Taiwan International Cooperation Alliance (TICA). It supports students from listed partner countries to take bachelor's (diplomatic-partner countries only), master's and Ph.D. programmes taught in English at Taiwanese universities. It pays tuition, credit fees, dormitory housing, insurance, textbook costs, round-trip economy flights and a monthly allowance. Applications for the 2027 intake run from 1 December 2026 to 15 March 2027; the details below follow the 2026 guidebook, the latest published.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants must be citizens of a country on the List of Countries Eligible for TaiwanICDF Scholarship and meet any criteria set by their own country or government. In the 2026 guidebook the list is: Belize, Guatemala, Mexico; Haiti, St. Kitts and Nevis, St. Lucia, St. Vincent and the Grenadines; Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay; Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Hungary, Kosovo, Latvia, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Serbia; Cote d'Ivoire, Djibouti, Eswatini, Ethiopia, Kenya, Senegal, South Africa, Somaliland, Tanzania, Uganda; Fiji, India, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Marshall Islands, Myanmar, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Philippines, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Tuvalu, Vietnam; Jordan, Mongolia, Russia, Turkiye. Applicants from other countries cannot apply. Senegalese applicants contact the Taipei representation in Cote d'Ivoire, and Tanzanian applicants the Taiwan representative office in Somaliland.

Bachelor's programmes are open only to applicants from countries with diplomatic relations with Taiwan. In the 2026 list these are Belize, Guatemala, Haiti, St. Kitts and Nevis, St. Lucia, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, Paraguay, Eswatini, Marshall Islands, Palau and Tuvalu.

Applicants must not be Taiwanese nationals or overseas compatriot students. They must meet the admission requirements of the partner university and programme they apply to, and be able to meet the requirements for a Resident Visa (code FS) and an Alien Resident Certificate. They must not hold another Taiwan government-sponsored scholarship (such as the Taiwan Scholarship) in the year the award starts, and must not apply for a TaiwanICDF scholarship in unbroken succession: for the 2026 round, those who had held a TaiwanICDF, MOFA Taiwan Scholarship or MOE scholarship had to graduate before 31 July 2025. They must never have had a scholarship revoked by a Taiwan government agency or related institution, or been expelled from a Taiwanese university. The highest-level diploma must be provided before 31 July of the enrolment year, otherwise the scholarship is cancelled (an applicant who cannot get the certificate by then may apply the next year). Passport valid for at least 24 months. Someone already studying in another country in another programme cannot apply; the scholarship is only for students at TICA partner schools and programmes.

The TaiwanICDF sets no English test requirement itself and no age limit, and asks for no recommendation letters, but each programme may set its own language, academic or recommendation requirements. An applicant may apply to only one programme at one TICA university each year. Winners must return home after the programme, may not work outside what Taiwan labour law allows, and must keep satisfactory grades.
age_experience_notes: The guidebook FAQ says there is no age limit and applicants are evaluated comprehensively. No work-experience requirement is stated by the TaiwanICDF; programmes may set their own.
funding_summary: For the award period the TaiwanICDF provides: round-trip economy flights, dormitory housing, tuition, credit fees, insurance, textbook costs (with the institute director's approval) and a monthly allowance of NT$15,000 (bachelor's), NT$18,000 (master's) or NT$20,000 (Ph.D.). The Ph.D. award period is four years. The guidebook states no award period for bachelor's or master's programmes. The award cannot be extended or deferred; extra study time is at the student's own expense. The first month's allowance is paid in full on arrival; there is no separate relocation allowance.
programmes_note: The 2026 guidebook lists the programmes open for application: 3 Ph.D., 27 master's and 4 bachelor's entries. All training is in English. An applicant picks one programme at one TICA university and cannot change it after submitting; accepted students cannot move to another programme, or the scholarship is cancelled.  The 2027 list was not online at the time of reading.
institutions_note: Partner universities of the Taiwan International Cooperation Alliance (TICA) with programmes in 2026: National Pingtung University of Science and Technology, National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University, Taipei Medical University, National Taiwan Ocean University, National Chung Hsing University, National Chengchi University, National Tsing Hua University, National Taiwan Normal University, Ming Chuan University, National Kaohsiung University of Hospitality and Tourism, National Central University, National Sun Yat-sen University, Yuan Ze University, National Cheng Kung University, National Dong Hwa University, National Chung Cheng University, Taipei National University of the Arts, National Taipei University, National Taiwan University of Science and Technology, National Chi Nan University. Applicants must also apply to the university and meet its documents and deadline.

benefits.limit_text: Round-trip economy class airfare, most direct flights
benefits.conditions: Arranged and paid by the TaiwanICDF; no stopover fee is available. After graduation (before the end of August of the final year) one economy single-trip ticket home is provided; for Ph.D. students it is still given if completion takes up to six years of continuous study. Visa fees are the recipient's.
All students must live in the student dormitories.

benefits.limit_text: Tuition fee and credit fees as required by the student's university
benefits.conditions: Credit fees vary with the number of credits registered.

benefits.limit_text: Medical insurance up to a premium of NT$30,000 (life insurance not included); accident insurance up to a premium of NT$2,000,000
benefits.conditions: From the seventh month in Taiwan the TaiwanICDF also pays enrolment in National Health Insurance. Insurance fees are covered for the whole programme in addition to the mandatory student safety insurance.

benefits.limit_text: NT$15,000 per month (bachelor's); NT$18,000 per month (master's); NT$20,000 per month (Ph.D.)
benefits.conditions: Deposited monthly into the student's local bank account for food and miscellaneous living expenses. The first month's allowance is paid in full after arrival. If the final departure is on or before the 15th of the month, half is paid for that month. No allowance is paid for time outside Taiwan beyond two consecutive months in a semester. The TaiwanICDF may suspend it for one to three months for misconduct.
Textbooks required by instructors are subject to the approval of the institute director. The orientation arranged by the TaiwanICDF is paid by it.

benefits.limit_text: Visa fees, passport costs, and any expenses above the Scope of Scholarship
benefits.conditions: Visa fees (including transit visas) are paid by the recipient or employer. There is no separate relocation allowance.

requirements.text: Online application in the TaiwanICDF Scholarship Online Application System, complete and accurate, submitted by the deadline (the guidebook does not itemise the uploads; each country office may also ask for hard or soft copies).
Separate application and all documents required by the partner university and programme, before that university's admissions deadline. Each programme's page lists its own documents.
Highest-level diploma, provided before 31 July of the enrolment year, or the scholarship is cancelled.
Valid passport (or equivalent travel document) good for at least 24 months before its expiry date.
Physical examination form, whose information must be genuine (referred to in the Terms of the Program; the form itself was not opened).

Document authentication: the Taiwan embassy or office tells you whether your documents need authentication by the Bureau of Consular Affairs. Original documents certified by a public notary, a supplementary copy of each, and original identity papers are required for that.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only if the embassy or office says authentication is needed.

requirements.text: Signed Consent Form from the Acceptance Letter, signed in the presence of an official of the Taiwan embassy, consulate or representative office.
English proficiency test: not required by the TaiwanICDF; the partner programme may require one.
Recommendation letters: not required by the TaiwanICDF; check the programme's admission requirements.

application_steps.title: Fill in the TaiwanICDF online application
application_steps.detail: Apply in the TaiwanICDF Scholarship Online Application System. The 2027 window is 1 December 2026 to 15 March 2027 (the 2026 window was 1 December 2025 to 15 March 2026). Information must be accurate and complete or the application is not processed. You can apply to one programme at one TICA university per year, cannot change it after submitting, and must redo the whole application each year. The TaiwanICDF charges no application fee.

application_steps.title: Apply to the partner university too
application_steps.detail: Submit the university's own application and documents before its admission deadline. A successful application needs the online application, the university's procedure, and all documents sent to the Taiwan embassy, consulate or representative office in your country when it asks. Universities may charge their own fees.

application_steps.title: Contact the Taiwan embassy or representative office
application_steps.detail: The office in your country handles your file. Whether hard or soft copies are needed depends on each office. It does a first review against the TaiwanICDF's eligibility and selection criteria and verifies your credentials.

application_steps.title: First review by the embassy, list sent by 31 March
application_steps.detail: The embassy or office reviews applicants and sends its list of recommended applicants to the TaiwanICDF no later than 31 March each year.

application_steps.title: Second review by the partner university and the TaiwanICDF
application_steps.detail: An academic committee of the partner university, together with TaiwanICDF representatives, reviews the qualified applicants using the university's criteria and the TaiwanICDF's eligibility and selection criteria (a joint recruitment committee).

application_steps.title: Announcement by 10 June and acceptance letter
application_steps.detail: In principle the TaiwanICDF announces recipients no later than 10 June each year and sends acceptance letters through the Taiwan embassy or office you applied to. Admission to the university alone does not mean you hold the scholarship; only an acceptance letter from the TaiwanICDF does.

application_steps.title: Sign the consent form and confirm your place
application_steps.detail: Read the consent form, sign it in front of an embassy official and return it through the office. Email the signed Acceptance Letter to the TaiwanICDF through the office in your country. Provide your highest-level diploma before 31 July of the enrolment year.

application_steps.title: Prepare passport and visa, then fly to Taiwan
application_steps.detail: Passport valid at least 24 months. Show the Acceptance Letter when applying for the Taiwan visa and check it covers the whole programme. The TaiwanICDF books your economy flight; arrival is arranged for early September, and a TaiwanICDF representative takes you to your accommodation. A very late arrival may lead to cancellation of your place and flight.

application_steps.title: Orientation and study
application_steps.detail: The TaiwanICDF runs an orientation on rules, Taiwanese customs and culture. Staff hold a monitoring meeting with the institute director at the end of each semester. Recipients may do part-time work only within Taiwan's employment law, may not transfer to another field, and must join TaiwanICDF activities.

application_steps.title: Keep the conditions and return home
application_steps.detail: Unsatisfactory grades (an average of 70 out of 100 or lower for undergraduates, 80 or lower for postgraduates, or failing a thesis or too many modules), political activity, unauthorised work, misconduct, transfer of field or a missing diploma can lead to suspension or termination. Recipients who drop out without consent must repay airfare and allowances. After finishing they agree to return to their home country and the TaiwanICDF hopes they join the alumni society.

fetch_problems: Direct download from the TaiwanICDF site timed out repeatedly; the two PDFs were obtained through the fetch tool's saved copies and read.
The per-programme 'Application Information and Program Introduction' pages were not opened, so programme-level document lists, entry requirements and deadlines are not captured.
The 2027 versions of the guidebook, the 'Programs Available for Application' PDF and the eligible-country list were not published when read; the 2026 documents were used as the basis.
notes: Corrections to stored data: the 2026 guidebook gives the amounts the stored text said were missing: allowance NT$15,000 (bachelor's), NT$18,000 (master's), NT$20,000 (Ph.D.). It also lists dormitory housing, tuition, credit fees and textbook costs as provided, and says housing is dormitory-only.
Stored claim 'bachelor's places reserved for diplomatic partners' is confirmed by the guidebook (FAQ and country list).
Stored rule 'unsatisfactory = average 70/100 or lower for undergraduates, 80/100 or lower for postgraduates' is confirmed in the Terms of the Program.

The guidebook says 32 programmes are offered in 2026, while the programme pages list 34 entries (3 Ph.D., 27 master's, 4 bachelor's). The entries are copied as listed. Only the first 25 master's entries are copied; the 26th and 27th are the Taiwan Tech semiconductor institute and the NCNU business administration master's programme.
The programme page states the 2027 application window is 1 December 2026 to 15 March 2027, matching the stored milestone.
